text:
maria: Kicking off a replay run on a 24h production trace dump (anonymized). Goal: reproduce kernel selection + batching decisions and KV cache warmup behavior so we can compare p50/p95/p99 to prod. Thoughts on sampling and parity checks?
raj: +1. Suggest stratified sampling by request size and model family. Keep full tail (largest 5%) un-sampled for stress scenarios.
oliver: For anonymization we hashed user_id and redacted prompt-level PII. Also removed full-document contexts > 32k. That keeps structure but avoids leakage.
sasha: Important: deterministic mode for kernels. We need to run with fixed seeds and pinned CUDA/cuBLAS kernels where possible to avoid FP nondeterminism across runs.
maria: Agreed. We'll run two passes: (A) best-effort deterministic config (pinned kernels, float32 path) and (B) production-ish config (autoselect kernels, quantized paths) so we can do apples-to-apples and apples-to-prod comparisons.
raj: How are we validating parity? Bitwise output parity is unrealistic for (B). Propose we compare token-level divergence distributions, per-request latency deltas, and KV hit/miss heatmaps. Also flag any >5% change in p99.
oliver: Also capture per-step kernel choice logs and batch composition timeline. We can diff kernel selection counts between runs to find heuristics regressions.
sasha: KV cache warmup: replay should preserve session affinity ordering so warmups happen similar to prod. For sampled sessions we should keep original inter-request intervals, not normalize them. Interval stretching will change batching.
perf-bot: replay-job queued: id=3319, config=24h-anon-stratified, seeds=[42], pinned_kernels=true. ETA ~45m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
infra-ci: queued onto cluster gpu-pool-3. Will report node-level metrics (GPU util, PCIe, mem) back to job.
maria: For logfile schema include: request_id (hashed), model, input_len, output_len, kernel_choice, batch_size, kv_hit, latency_ms, cpu_ms, gpu_ms. Add a "reason" tag when fallback occurs.
raj: Add a quick check: run a short micro-benchmark snapshot that exercises long-context KV reuse (200 tokens per step) to validate cache eviction policy before full run.
oliver: Noted perf regression guard: if p99 latency regresses >10% vs baseline or kernel selection shifts >20% to slower kernels, auto-abort and capture full perf trace.
sasha: For output comparison, use normalized BLEU-ish token overlap for generation tasks and exact-match rates for deterministic RPC responses. Record divergence buckets: 0, 1–2, 3–5, >5 tokens different.
maria: After run, generate these artifacts: 1) kernel_selection_deltas.csv 2) batching_time_series.json 3) kv_warmup_heatmap.png 4) token_divergence_hist.csv 5) perf-profiles/trace-3319/*.svg
raj: One more: annotate samples that hit quantized paths vs float32 separately. Mixing them skews latency distributions.
perf-bot: replay-job started: id=3319. Logs to /replays/3319/*.log.
maria: I'll wait for the job artifacts and then schedule a 30-min sync to prioritize fixes. Thanks team.
oliver: If we see nondeterministic flips, I'll instrument kernel-level hashes to help root-cause.
sasha: Also recommend a small follow-up: run identical trace on a different instance type to rule out infra-induced noise (PCIe or driver differences).
raj: Sounds good. Thanks all.
perf-bot: replay-job finished: id=3319, status=completed, duration=42m, artifacts=21 files.
maria: Got the artifacts. Pulling kernel_selection_deltas.csv now -> looks like batch selection bias towards larger batches at 12:14UTC, investigating.
raj: Ping if you need me to run a focused repro on the candidate commit.
maria: Will do — filing an internal issue with initial diffs and attaching the top 20 requests showing divergent kernel choices.
